title: In an Emergency Situation the Facilitator may compress Root Edit timelines and withhold the announcement if disclosure would endanger Osero or its users
content:
A.6.1.1.7.2.2.2.2.1.2.3.1 grants the Operational Facilitator discretion to accelerate governance: "In an Emergency Situation, as defined by the Sky Core Atlas in A.1.9.1.1 ... the Operational Facilitator may allow a Root Edit to occur more quickly than the timeline specified above."

Two features of the drafting matter. First, the trigger is not defined locally — it borrows the Atlas-wide definition of Emergency Situations, so Osero cannot widen its own emergency conditions by editing its Artifact. Second, the compression is of *timeline*, not of the steps themselves: the seven-day review and three-day poll can shrink, but the text does not authorize skipping the Facilitator review or the holder vote outright.

The disclosure obligation is the weakest part. The Facilitator "should" announce the decision and reasoning publicly "where feasible" — hedged language — and is excused entirely "unless doing so would endanger Osero or its users."

That exception is defensible for live exploits, where announcing an emergency edit telegraphs the vulnerability. But it is self-judged by the actor exercising the power, at exactly the moment normal procedural checks are relaxed. The result is a window in which one actor can shorten a constitutional amendment process and decline to say why, with accountability arriving only retrospectively through the Data Repository record.
description: Emergency powers attach to the Atlas-wide definition of Emergency Situations, and the transparency obligation is qualified twice — "where feasible" and by a danger exception.
